public_rationale: The historical evidence points in different directions without settling the sentence. Workplace research found concrete benefits, and Adobe described licensed training. A contemporary survey found infrequent use, while investment analysis questioned returns. Firefly's use of other generators' outputs complicates its provenance. These findings neither establish necessary theft and permanent unsustainability nor justify treating every concern as false. A mixed grade would overstate how directly the evidence tests the unspecified comparisons.
limitations: Specific workplace benefits do not establish industry-wide profitability.
Company provenance statements are not independent audits.
The adoption survey covers six countries and mainly identifiable standalone tools.
The provenance complication is documented here through a secondary account.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Generative AI was always unsustainable, depended on stolen training data, and had vague utility and overstated ubiquity.

statement.excerpt: Generative AI was always unsustainable, always dependent on reams of training data that necessitated stealing from millions of people, its utility vague and its ubiquity overstated.

from_speaker: training data that necessitated stealing from millions of people
our_interpretation: Read as a description of generative AI through publication, not a forecast about its later development. 'Always' supplies no starting date.
The ordinary reading concerns economic viability, dependence on taking creators' work without permission, demonstrated practical benefits, and actual adoption compared with publicity.
Unauthorized use, copyright infringement and theft are not interchangeable legal findings. Licensing claims alone do not establish complete training-data provenance.
Evidence of particular useful applications bears on the utility assertion but does not by itself settle the broader assessment.
No particular adoption claim, profitability threshold or definition of sustainability is supplied.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence covering the historical industry establishes dependence on unauthorized material, an economically unviable business model, weak practical benefits, and adoption materially below identifiable contemporary claims.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable historical evidence directly defeats an asserted necessity or establishes that the claimed lack of clear utility or exaggeration of adoption is materially false. Narrow counterexamples must not be treated as proof of industry-wide profitability or clean provenance.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Complete provenance and permission records, comparable historical financial evidence, and an identifiable adoption comparison would resolve the factual components. A single overall grade also requires a defensible treatment of the undefined evaluative terms.
